facts.claim: Construction of the Suez Canal lasted from 1859 to 1869; it officially opened on 17 November 1869.
The canal is about 193 km (120 miles) long, between Port Said and Suez.
From the Persian Gulf to northern Europe, the route around Africa is about 21,000 km; through the Suez Canal about 12,000 km.

sources.title: Geographical Impacts of the Suez and Panama Canals

facts.claim: The Suez Canal handled roughly 12% to 15% of global trade in 2023.

sources.title: UN: Global trade is being disrupted by Red Sea attacks, war in Ukraine and low water in Panama Canal (UNCTAD briefing)

facts.claim: The canal carries about 30% of global container traffic.

sources.title: A lifeline under threat: Why the Suez Canal's security matters for the world

facts.claim: The Suez Crisis took place in October–November 1956.
In March 2021 the container ship Ever Given ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days.

sources.title: Ever Given container ship on the move, ending a six-day jam

facts.claim: On 28 March 2021 at least 369 ships were queuing to pass through the canal.
